prompt: Which sentence has a spelling error?
choices: Leo felt a pang of conscience after he took the last slice of pizza.
The mischievious puppy chewed through two of my sneakers while we were out at dinner.
The store will guarantee the repair work for one full year.
Nora tends to exaggerate when she talks about camp.
correct_answer: The mischievious puppy chewed through two of my sneakers while we were out at dinner.
spelling_pattern: extra syllable/vowel inserted before the -ous suffix (mischievous, not mischievious)

student_error.Leo felt a pang of conscience after he t: conscience has an unusual sc + ie spelling; students expect conshence or consience
student_error.The store will guarantee the repair work: the silent u after g and the double e look wrong to students who write garantee
student_error.Nora tends to exaggerate when she talks: students are unsure about the double g and often write exagerate

explanation: Mischievous has three syllables and no i before -ous; mischievious is a common misspelling. Conscience, guarantee and exaggerate are spelled correctly.

prompt: Which sentence has a spelling error?

correct_answer: Sam met a new aquaintance at the fair.
spelling_pattern: silent letter dropped in a cluster: acquaintance has a c before the q

student_error.We walked past the old cemetery on Elm S: the unstressed vowel in the third syllable is hard to hear, and students often write cemetary
student_error.Would you recommend this book to a frien: students often double the c or drop an m (reccomend, recomend), so the correct form looks doubtful
student_error.There was a noticeable change in the wea: students are taught to drop the final e before -able, so keeping the e looks wrong

explanation: Acquaintance needs a silent c before the q (ac-quaint); aquaintance drops it. Cemetery, recommend and noticeable (which keeps the e to keep the c soft) are correct.
